section.title: Introduction
section.p: This module provides support for portable machines. The SWIs listed are not normally intended to be issued from user programs, they will normally be issued by other modules in the system.

service-definition.name: Portable
service-definition.description: Portable state change request, or information

entry.register-use:
Sub-reason code:
Hardware is about to be powered down Hardware has been powered up Tidy up Device is about to enter a stopped state (frozen) Device has left stopped state (awakened) Device wishes to be stopped (frozen) Reserved for future expansion

Bit mask of which ports are being powered down (if R2 = 0) (each bit set indicates port is being powered down) or bit mask of which ports have been powered up (if R2 = 1) (each bit set indicates port has been powered up)

exit.register-use: 0 if R3 = 0, else preserved to pass on
Bit mask of which ports may be powered down or up (each bit set indicates no objection to change of state)

use.p: This call is issued before power is removed or after power is reapplied to the following:

If a module wishes to prevent hardware being powered down it should clear the appropriate bit or bits in R3. In addition, if the resulting value in R3 is now zero, the module should claim the service by setting R1 to zero. (This is to prevent the call being unnecessarily passed round the rest of the modules). Otherwise the service should be passed on by preserving R1.
This service call should never be claimed.

service-definition.name: Portable
service-definition.description: Hardware is about to be powered down

entry.register-use: Bit mask of which ports are being powered down (each bit set indicates port is being powered down)

exit.register-use: 0 if R3 = 0, else preserved to pass on
Bit mask of which ports may be powered down (each bit set indicates no objection to change of state)

use.p: This call is issued before power is removed from the following:

If a module wishes to prevent hardware being powered down it should clear the appropriate bit or bits in R3. In addition, if the resulting value in R3 is now zero, the module should claim the service by setting R1 to zero. (This is to prevent the call being unnecessarily passed round the rest of the modules). Otherwise the service should be passed on by preserving R1.
This service call should never be claimed.

entry.register-use: Bit mask of which ports have been powered up (each bit set indicates port has been powered up)

exit.register-use: 0 if R3 = 0, else preserved to pass on

use.p: This call is issued after power is reapplied to the following:
The service should be passed on by preserving R1.

service-definition.name: Portable
service-definition.description: Device is about to enter a stopped state (frozen)

use.p: This call is issued before the device is put into a stopped mode where the CPU core has been disabled. RAM continues to be refreshed and the system will probably be woken up at some future point. It is possible that the power may fail on the device before it is awakened. In such cases, the device may next be activated from a hard reset condition.

entry.register-use:
Failure code:
Freeze was successful and has now returned Freeze failed to halt IDE devices Freeze failed to halt sound system Freeze failed to halt display Freeze failed to halt other devices (FDC, Econet, etc) Freeze failed to halt some device Freeze failed to enter the suspend state Reserved failure states for future expansion

use.p: This call is issued after the device returns from a stopped state. It may never have physically stopped the CPU if some part of the system failed to be shut down. In such cases, it may not be necessary to fully resynchronise the environment - for example, network connections may still be active.

exit.register-use: 0 if call is being claimed to prevent freeze, preserved to accept freeze

use.p: This call is issued before the device is stopped. Any module wishing to object to the request may claim the service.
This SWI controls the processor speed, which is reduced when the system is idle in order to save power.
The new speed is calculated as follows:

extended-example.userinput: new speed = (old speed AND R1) EOR R0

swi-definition.name: Portable_Control
swi-definition.description: Control various power control and miscellaneous bits

use.p: This SWI controls various power control and miscellaneous bits in the portable machine.
The new control is calculated as follows:

extended-example.userinput: new control = (old control AND R1) EOR R0

use.p: The bits in control are as follows:

bitfield-table.bit: Power to external video display enabled
Power to serial buffer and oscillator enabled

Video clock control:
External clock input Crystal oscillator, divided by 2 Crystal oscillator Reserved, do not use
Set: 2 extra lines on display. Clear: 1 extra line on display
Set: 2 DRAMs used for dual panel. Clear: 1 DRAM used for dual panel
LCD palette set up for inverse video
Power to external keyboard and mouse enabled

use.p: Reserved bits must not be modified, nor assumed to read any particular value.
Note that the 82C711 has one oscillator which is used by the serial sub-unit and by the floppy disc controller (FDC). Power to the oscillator is removed only if bits 3 and 14 are both clear.
On some computers the power to the oscillator cannot be removed because the same oscillator drives other parts of the system (eg IOEB).
If this call results in bits 0, 3 or 14 changing (i.e. power being removed or applied to the serial buffer/oscillator, Econet or FDC oscillator), then is issued (see ).
This SWI reads Battery Management Unit variables. Any variable which is not supported will return an error.
The BMU variable numbers are:

value-table.value: Version number and memory map of BMU microcode

use.p: The flag bits of variable 10 are:

bitfield-table.bit: Battery present (set when battery is present, whether in use, charging or idle)
Power connected (set when external power is available, whether charging or not)

use.p: Reading any variable except the flags (variable 10) will enable IRQs (the flags are read from a soft copy).

Variables 0-11 were implemented within the A4 version of the Portable module. Variables 12-20 and selected variables from 0-11 were implemented within the Stork version of the Portable module. Variables 21-22 are implemented within the Virtual RiscPC version of the Portable module. Variables 0-4, 10, 11 and 14 are provided by the A9 version of the Portable.

Despite this, clients should not expect any particular variables to be provided by a given implementation as hardware capabilities and software implementation may change. Clients should always attempt to read the value and take appropriate action if a failure occurs.

Variables which are not supported will return with the V flag set and R0 pointing to a standard error block. Applications trying to use the more advanced features and finding they are not available should attempt to fall back to earlier methods.
This SWI writes Battery Management Unit variables.
The variable numbers are as for Portable_ReadBMUVariable. Variables not marked with a 'W' should not be written.

swi-definition.name: Portable_CommandBMU
swi-definition.description: Issue a command to the Battery Management Unit

entry.register-use:
Reason code:
Remove power Reserved Reserved Set autostart (R1 = delay in minutes - 1; eg 0 for a 1 minute delay) Turn off AC power Turn on AC power Disable power management status

use.p: This SWI issues a command to the Battery Management Unit. The values of variables after a command may not change immediately after this command is issued.

swi-definition.name: Portable_ReadFeatures
swi-definition.description: Read the feature set of the portable module

exit.register-use:
Features of the portable module:
Portable_Speed SWI is implemented Reserved, must be zero Portable_Idle SWI is implemented Portable_Stop SWI is implemented Reserved, must be zero

use.p: This SWI is used to read the features provided by the Portable module. Where this module is not present, or this SWI generates an error if called, clients should treat the features as being 0.

swi-definition.name: Portable_Idle
swi-definition.description: Inform the portable module that the system is currently idle

use.p: This SWI places the system into idle mode. The CPU clock is stopped, but all other clocks run normally. This means the Video display and all the IO channels are active, the DRAM is refreshed, but the system consumes less power as the CPU is inactive. The CPU remains in this state until it receives a FIQ or IRQ interrupt (eg from the keyboard, floppy, centi-second timer etc).
Essentially it requests that the environment be stopped until 'something interesting' happens.

exit.register-use:
Reason for wake up:
Keyboard interrupt RTC timer interrupt Reserved

use.p: This SWI places the machine into a 'standby' state, from which it can be awoken by certain interrupts. DRAM is set to self-refresh, and the system placed into stop mode (all clocks are stopped). Execution continues only on receipt of an external wakeup event from the keyboard or real-time-clock. Normal FIQ or IRQ or centi-second timer events cannot happen because the IO system is not clocked.

Freezing of the machine may be prevented by modules through the service call . This service is issued prior to attempts to freeze the machine. If no clients object to this service, will be issued and the machine shut down. Upon an interrupt, will be issued to notify clients that the power has been restored and a period of time has elapsed during which interrupts have not happened.

swi-definition.name: Portable_Status
swi-definition.description: Read the status of the Portable environment

exit.register-use:
Status of the Portable environment:
Device is currently docked Device has external floppy disc drive connected Device has tracker ball connected (rather than mouse) Device has internal display in use Reserved, must be zero

use.p: This SWI is used to read the status of the Portable environment. This allows applications to modify their behaviour, or for modules to configure their operations based on the environment in which the device is situated.
